cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (no config - demo: Example Co., a fictional company, with invented numbers)
REVENUE-TO-PIPELINE PLAN
Period                       Q1 2027, 3 months
Revenue target               $600,000
Expected from open pipeline  $120,000 (your figure)
New revenue still to win     $480,000
Average deal size            $25,000
Rates                        from last period's counts
STAGE            RATE ON       EXACT    NEEDED  PER MONTH
Opportunities      25.0%        76.8        80       26.7
RATE ON is the rate from each stage to the next one listed.
Counts round up at each stage, from the whole number below it:
you cannot win 0.4 of a deal. EXACT is before rounding.
PER MONTH is the rounded count spread evenly over the period.
LAST PERIOD
Leads 2,400 > MQLs 840 > SQLs 300 > Opportunities 120 > Wins 30
MONTHLY GAP (need per month vs what you produce per month now)
Leads          need 533.3, have 450: short 83.3 (15.6% of need)
MQLs           need 186.7, have 160: short 26.7 (14.3% of need)
SQLs           need 66.7, have 70: covered
Opportunities  need 26.7, have 20: short 6.7 (25.0% of need)
Largest gap for its size: Opportunities (25.0% short)
LEAD TIME
At a 75-day cycle from a new lead to a win, the leads behind this
period's wins have to be created between 75 days before the period
starts and 75 days before it ends (the period is about 91 days,
counting a month as 365/12 days). Leads created in the last 75 days of
the period close after it ends. This treats every deal as taking the
same 75 days; real cycles vary.
NOTES
- Revenue expected from open pipeline is your own figure and is
subtracted as given. If it is the full value of open deals rather than
a weighted forecast, the plan understates what is needed.
- Rates come from last period's counts at each stage. Deals that crossed
from one period into the next make these rates approximate; a cohort
view (what share of a period's leads became wins, however long it
took) is more exact when you have it.
- Rounded up to whole wins, 20 wins at the average deal size bring in
$500,000, more than the $480,000 still to win.

LEAD TIME
At a 120-day cycle from a new SQL to a win, the SQLs behind this
period's wins have to be created between 120 days before the period
starts and 120 days before it ends (the period is about 61 days,
counting a month as 365/12 days). The cycle is as long as the period
or longer, so all of them have to be created before the period starts.
This treats every deal as taking the same 120 days; real cycles vary.

cases.name: bad input: several errors named at once
cases.source: unknown field, text for a number, zero deal size, part month, rate above 1
stderr: error: Unknown field "foo". Allowed: target, dealSize, periodMonths, expected, rates, last, current, salesCycleDays, period, currency.
error: "target" must be a number (got "abc").
error: "dealSize" must be above 0 (got 0).
error: "periodMonths" must be a whole number from 1 to 36 (got 2.5).
error: Rate "oppsToWins" must be above 0 and at most 1 (got 1.5). Write 35% as 0.35.
Run --help for the schema, or --demo for a worked example.

cases.name: bad input: broken chain of rates
cases.source: leadsToMqls then sqlsToOpps leaves a hole at MQLs to SQLs
stderr: error: The rates must form one chain: "leadsToMqls" ends at MQLs, but the next rate, "sqlsToOpps", starts at SQLs.
Run --help for the schema, or --demo for a worked example.

cases.name: bad input: chain does not reach wins
cases.source: the last rate must end at wins
stderr: error: The chain must end at wins: the last rate, "mqlsToSqls", ends at SQLs. Add the rates from SQLs down to wins, such as "sqlsToOpps" and "oppsToWins".
Run --help for the schema, or --demo for a worked example.

cases.name: bad input: counts grow down the funnel
stderr: error: Wins (12) is more than Opportunities (10) last period; each stage should be no larger than the one above it.
Run --help for the schema, or --demo for a worked example.

cases.name: bad input: rates and counts both given
cases.source: the engine will not choose between them
stderr: error: Give "rates" or "last", not both: the engine would not know which to plan from.
Run --help for the schema, or --demo for a worked example.

cases.name: bad input: no rates at all

Run --help for the schema, or --demo for a worked example.
